summary: President Barack Obama hosted Super Bowl‑winning New England Patriots at the White House, opening his remarks with a deflategate joke. Coach Bill Belichick responded with a thumbs‑down, and the team—absent MVP quarterback Tom Brady—received a custom jersey and football from the president. The joke drew groans from the players and highlighted Brady’s absence due to “family commitments.”
reference:
Brady cited 'prior family commitments' in bowing out of meeting with Obama .
Has been to the White House to meet President George W. Bush for previous Super Bowl wins .

summary: The White House announced that Adam Gadahn, a 36‑year‑old American who served as al Qaeda’s English‑language propagandist, was killed in a U.S. counterterrorism operation in January. The statement said Gadahn and fellow U.S. citizen al‑Qaeda operative Ahmed Farouq were not specifically targeted, and the strike that killed Farouq also killed U.S. hostage Warren Weinstein and Italian hostage Giovanni Lo Porto. Gadahn’s death ends the life of one of al Qaeda’s most prominent Western spokespeople.
reference:
In his final known video, Adam Gadahn called for governments of Pakistan and Saudi Arabia to be overthrown .
He was raised in California and said he was of Jewish ancestry .
He converted to Islam in 1995, left U.S. in 1998 and joined al Qaeda, becoming a spokesman .

summary: John Barnes and Jamie Redknapp teamed up to perform a rendition of the Sugarhill Gang’s “Rapper’s Delight” in a spoof “Britain’s Got Sporting Talent” sketch for Sky’s upcoming series A League Of Their Own. The act featured Barnes in a hoodie, hat and sunglasses with backing dancers, and Redknapp joining him midway to share the mic. Their performance entertained the audience and highlighted the pair’s unexpected rap abilities.

Barnes' ex-Liverpool team-mate Jamie Redknapp joins in halfway through .
Barnes featured on Anfield Rap and World in Motion in the past .

summary: John Higgins and Graeme Dott led Scotland’s charge at the Betfred World Championship, each winning their first‑round matches. Higgins defeated Robert Milkins 10‑5 with high breaks, while Dott edged Ricky Walden 10‑8. Their victories highlighted Higgins’s return to form and renewed hopes of a fifth world title.
reference:
John Higgins beats Robert Milkins 10-5 to reach second round .
Higgins says he would love to challenge for World title again .
But the 39-year-old admits there are many more favoured players .
Graeme Dott sees off Ricky Walden 10-8 .

summary: Arsenal will wear their yellow and blue away kit in the FA Cup final against Aston Villa on May 30 after Villa won the pre‑match coin toss and selected their claret‑and‑blue home strip. The Gunners, who have won three of their five finals in the yellow‑blue colors, view the kit choice as a positive omen as they aim to retain the trophy. The match will kick off at 5

summary: Philippe Coutinho scored the only goal in Liverpool’s 1‑0 FA Cup replay win over Blackburn Rovers, with captain Jordan Henderson providing the assist. Despite having just become a father to a second daughter and missing a night’s sleep, Henderson played the full match and helped secure the victory. The win sends Liverpool to a Wembley semi‑final against Aston Villa.
reference:
Coutinho hit the only goal of the game as Liverpool beat Blackburn .
They will meet Aston Villa in the semi-finals a week on Sunday .

Boss Brendan Rodgers revealed Henderson had no thoughts about missing the match .
'He said to me, "Boss, as soon as the baby's out, I'll be coming back",' Rodgers explained .

summary: Men’s face product company West Coast Shaving released a project that digitally blends the faces of members from 30 legendary rock bands into single composite images. The mashups highlight recognizable features such as Kurt Cobain in Nirvana, Paul McCartney in The Beatles, and Eddie Van Halen in Van Halen, while other bands like U2 and the Rolling Stones appear more ambiguous. The company posted the images online, noting mixed results for groups such as KISS and ZZ Top.
reference:
Members of 30 rock band members merged into one face each .
Beatles look like Paul McCartney, Nirvana look like Kurt Cobain .
U2, Rolling Stones and Green Day are a bizarre blend .

summary: A dental assistant at an Aspen Dental office in Alabama forcibly removed a nine‑month‑old baby from his mother, Tayler Chaice Buzbee, while she was breastfeeding during a dental appointment. Buzbee said the employee took the infant without permission, leaving her feeling humiliated and prompting her to leave the clinic. Aspen Dental Management issued an apology, stating that no nursing mother should be made uncomfortable and that the incident is under investigation.
reference:
Mother-of-one Tayler Chaice Buzbee called Aspen Dental with toothache .
She was told only available appointment at the facility was in 20 minutes .
Had no time to find babysitter for baby son, Attley, so brought him along .
Started breastfeeding the nine-month-old in chair when he created a fuss .
But soon after, female employee 'took him out of her arms without asking'
Woman 'placed him in his stroller, saying breastfeeding was not allowed'
'I was humiliated, crying, and I felt embarrassed to be there,' said Tayler .
Aspen Dental has since apologized to Tayler and launched investigation .

summary: Police are investigating the theft of 12 prize‑winning guinea pigs from top breeder Tony Tancock’s outbuilding in Crediton, Devon, after a thief left eight ordinary rodents behind. Tancock, who has won national show accolades, suspects the theft was carried out by someone with expert knowledge of his prized cavies, though police have not ruled out a rival competitor. The animals have not been recovered and the investigation remains ongoing.
reference:
Heart-broken Tony Tancock, 56, has won prizes for specially-bred guinea pigs .
A thief stole a dozen of his best from his home in Devon and left eight behind .
Says only an expert could have targetted them and left ordinary ones behind .
'They knew exactly what they were looking for,' a devastated Tancock claimed .

summary: English Premiership clubs Bath, Northampton, Saracens and Wasps face away quarter‑final matches in the European Champions Cup against French and Irish powerhouses. Bookmakers predict defending champions Toulon will secure a third consecutive title, with Clermont as the primary challenger followed by Racing and Leinster. The English teams are described as heavy
reference:
It has been eight years since an English club triumphed in the European Champions Cup .
Despite four English teams in this year's quarter-finals, that hoodoo looks set to persist .
English clubs are nowhere near as well-resourced as French clubs .
In a World Cup year, it would be a huge boost to national morale if English clubs could progress further into the competition .

summary: Atlanta writer Alex Gray, 27, lost 160 lb—dropping from 354 lb to about 194 lb—in 20 months after being motivated by a friend's dramatic weight loss. He began walking, then running, and swapped high‑calorie meals for lean protein, sustaining the regimen despite previous failed attempts. The transformation left him healthier, more confident socially and professionally, and able to purchase off‑the‑rack clothing.
reference:
It took Atlanta-based writer Alex Gray 20 months to lose the weight from his 354lbs frame .

summary: Taxi driver Mohammed Nisar returned a rucksack containing £10,000 that passenger Adrian Quinn had forgotten in his cab after being dropped at Walsall train station. Quinn, who feared losing the money would ruin his sole‑trader business, thanked Nisar with a cash reward and invited him and his wife for a family meal. Nisar’s honesty earned him a reward, a new friendship, and he urged other drivers to return lost valuables.
reference:
Mohammed Nisar had been taking Adrian Quinn to Walsall train station .
Mr Quinn was carrying hefty sum as he'd just cashed inheritance cheque .
After realising he'd lost the money says he 'felt physically sick' and 'dazed'
Sole trader Mr Quinn gave cabbie a cash reward and invited him to dinner .

summary: The Pulitzer Prizes were announced, with Anthony Doerr’s novel “All the Light We Cannot See” winning the fiction award. The ceremony also honored Stephen Adly Guirgis’s play “Between Riverside and Crazy” for drama, Elizabeth Kolbert’s “The Sixth Extinction” for general nonfiction, and a range of works in history, biography, music and poetry. The awards, administered by Columbia University, recognize distinguished achievements in journalism and letters.
reference:
Anthony Doerr's "All the Light We Cannot See" wins Pulitzer for fiction .
Elizabeth Kolbert's "The Sixth Extinction" wins general nonfiction prize .

summary: Former NFL tight end Aaron Hernandez was found guilty by a jury of first‑degree murder for the 2013 killing of Odin Lloyd. The court also convicted him of unlawful possession of a firearm and ammunition, leading to a sentence of life imprisonment without the possibility of parole. Hernandez’s attorney maintained his client did not commit the crime, but the verdict reflected the prosecution’s circumstantial evidence.
reference:
Roxanne Jones: Jury right to find Hernandez guilty, but the waste of life for player and his victim is tragic .
She says NFL, Patriots knew his troubled past, but could not have predicted his actions, and both handled case well .

summary: A Brown University study compared nine frequent video gamers with nine non‑gamers on a two‑day visual texture‑discrimination task. The researchers found that gamers improved performance on both tasks (about 11‑15% gains), while non‑gamers only improved on the second task and performed worse on the first. The results suggest gamers may have a more efficient visual‑learning process, though the study cannot determine whether gaming causes the advantage or if naturally better learners are drawn to games.
reference:
Researchers at Brown University studied how people learned tasks .
It has already been shown gamers learn visual tasks better .
But in this study they had higher performance across two tasks .
'They may be in an expert category of visual processing,' said Dr Sasaki .

summary: The 2015 Sunday Times Sport Rich List placed Lewis Hamilton at the top with a £88 million fortune, keeping him Britain’s richest sportsperson. Wayne Rooney moved into second place with £72 million, overtaking Jenson Button who fell to third with £71 million. The list also ranked Andy Murray fourth (£48 million) and placed other athletes and managers such as Steven Gerrard, Rio Ferdinand and Jose Mourinho further down.
reference:
Lewis Hamilton's fortune has spiralled by £20m to £88m in the past year .

The Manchester United captain's fortune is up £12m to £72m .

summary: Veteran actor Robert Hardy, 89, is auctioning more than 200 antiques, books and collectibles from his personal collection in a £100,000 sale at Dominic Winter in South Cerney, Gloucestershire. The items, including a hand‑painted Battle of Agincourt diorama, a yew longbow and numerous paintings, furniture and weapons, will be offered in 238 lots on Saturday. Hardy said downsizing his home makes him sad but hopes new owners will enjoy the pieces as he has.
reference:

summary: A Russian Udaloy‑class destroyer, accompanied by a tanker and a support ship, entered the English Channel while two long‑range Tu‑95 “Bear” bombers flew close to British airspace. The Royal Navy dispatched the frigate HMS Argyll to monitor the ships, and RAF Typhoon fighters from Lossiemouth scrambled to escort the bombers away. The Russian vessels and aircraft were tracked and escorted without incident, prompting British officials to view the incursions as a test of the United Kingdom’s defence response.
reference:
RAF jets escorted two Russian military aircraft close to UK airspace .
The Typhoons were scrambled from RAF Lossiemouth in Scotland .
HMS Argyle also monitoring three Russian ships in English Channel .
It comes at a time of heightened tension between Britain and Russia .

summary: Senator Marco Rubio announced his bid for the Republican presidential nomination, positioning himself as a youthful, Hispanic‑heritage candidate. His shift from comprehensive immigration reform to a stricter, piecemeal approach and his hard‑line stance on Cuba have alienated Latino voters and left him without a distinctive policy edge. Analysts conclude that these positions make his campaign a steep uphill battle for both the GOP nomination and broader Latino support.
reference:
Raul Reyes: In seeking Latino vote, Marco Rubio his own worst enemy on two key issues: immigration reform, Cuba relations .
He says on health care, climate change and other issues, he breaks from Latinos' positions. Polls show they don't favor him .

summary: Australian military adviser Dr. Adam Cobb was arrested in Portsmouth, New Hampshire, on charges of receiving and distributing child pornography after allegedly uploading images to Tumblr. Cobb, a former senior defence official in Australia and director of the Mahan Advanced Research Project at the U.S. Naval War College, appeared in federal court and was denied bail. If convicted, he faces a potential sentence of up to 20 years in prison.

summary: Petr Cech, Chelsea’s second‑choice goalkeeper, posted a YouTube video of himself drumming a cover of U2’s “Magnificent.” The Czech international shared the clip on Twitter, highlighting his musical hobby while remaining behind Thibaut Courtois in Jose Mourinho’s pecking order. Despite the showcase, Cech is expected to leave Stamford Bridge this summer, with Arsenal and Liverpool among clubs linked to him.

summary: A herd of about 15 buffalo that escaped from a farm in Schodack, New York, swam across the Hudson River and roamed onto the Thruway near Albany. Law enforcement, after consulting experts who ruled out tranquilizers and portable corrals, authorized three men hired by the farm to open fire on the animals in a stream near Coeymans. All of the escaped buffalo were shot dead.
reference:

However authorities took the decision to gun them down because they posed a danger to the public .

summary: A lawsuit filed by Christina Mejia alleges that Cook County sheriff’s deputies stripped her daughter Jessica Mejia’s body and took nude photographs after the 2009 car crash that killed her. The deputies contend the images were standard procedure that helped secure the conviction of driver Nicholas Sord, who received a 56‑month prison sentence for drunken driving. The civil case against the sheriff’s office is scheduled to go to trial next week

Cameron’s admission highlights his difficulty in impressing his children despite his attempts to project a modern, relatable image.

summary: A Philadelphia court sentenced three men to prison for the brutal assault, false imprisonment and forced tattooing of 53‑year‑old Greg Valecce in a basement “torture chamber” in 2014. Ringleader Corry “Corey” Campbell and accomplice Carl Halin each received 20‑year sentences, while Campbell’s girlfriend Sandra Ng was sentenced to 23 months, with two other participants still awaiting sentencing. The victims’ injuries included broken ribs, wrists and facial fractures, and the case concluded with all three pleading guilty.
